To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a blind DOAs estimate of narrowband signals can be obtained from the SOSs of the signals received by a vector-sensor array, via a low-rank CPD of the SOSs tensor.

1) a consistent blind DOAs estimate arises from the CPD of a tensor representation of SOSs of the signals measured by AVS arrays; 2) the MLE of the Gaussian model can be used as an improved DOAs estimate for non-Gaussian sources, which is optimal under the KLD covariance fitting criterion; and 3) the resulting estimates are considerably more accurate than those obtained with a previous blind DOAs estimate.
the SOSs tensor admits a natural low rank CPD and that this CPD is the solution to an equivalent joint diagonalization problem.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose and analyze a novel, consistent and computationally efficient blind DOAs estimate, which is optimal under the KLD covariance fitting criterion.

, by using a tensor decomposition approach to estimate the SOSs of the received signals, the proposed algorithm achieves a blind DOAs estimate that is optimal under the KLD covariance fitting criterion, and is thus more accurate than the state-of-the-art, while being computationally efficient.
we have proposed a novel blind DOAs estimate that is consistent, computationally tractable, and accurate for a wide range of signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tensor decomposition framework can be fruitfully applied to solve the blind DOAs estimation problem for AVS arrays.
the SOSs of the signals received by AVS arrays admit a natural tensor representation, which can be exploited in order to obtain improved DOA estimates.

the SOSs tensor structure of the signals received by AVS arrays provides a natural and effective means of estimating DOAs, without prior assumptions on either the array configuration or the signals’ statistical properties.
